label: June 2026 paper — gap-fill practice variants (booklet Q1–Q50)

items.stem: Let X and Y be independent, each exponential with parameter λ. Then P(X ≤ 1 | X + Y = 4) is
items.explanation: Given X + Y = s, X is uniform on (0, s) for independent exponentials with the same rate: the joint density λ²e^(−λs) does not depend on how s is split. So P(X ≤ 1 | X + Y = 4) = 1/4, whatever λ is. Trap: 1 − e^(−λ) is the unconditional P(X ≤ 1).

items.stem: A₁, A₂, …, Aₙ are independent events with P(Aᵢ) = 1 − 1/3^i, i = 1, 2, …, n. The probability that at least one of them occurs is
items.explanation: P(none occurs) = Π P(Aᵢᶜ) = Π 3^(−i) = 3^(−(1 + 2 + … + n)) = 3^(−n(n+1)/2), so P(at least one) = 1 − 1/3^(n(n+1)/2). Trap: 1 − 1/3ⁿ uses only the last event.

items.stem: X = (x₁, x₂, x₃)′ ~ N₃(μ, Σ) with μ = (1, 0, 2)′ and Σ = [[2, 1, 1], [1, 3, 1], [1, 1, 2]]. The conditional mean and covariance matrix of (x₂, x₃)′ given x₁ = 3 are
items.explanation: For a partitioned normal vector, E(X⁽²⁾ | x₁) = μ⁽²⁾ + Σ₂₁Σ₁₁⁻¹(x₁ − μ₁) and Cov(X⁽²⁾ | x₁) = Σ₂₂ − Σ₂₁Σ₁₁⁻¹Σ₁₂. With Σ₁₁ = 2, Σ₂₁ = (1, 1)′ and x₁ − μ₁ = 2 this gives (1, 3)′ and [[5/2, 1/2], [1/2, 3/2]]. Trap: the conditional covariance does not depend on the observed x₁, and it is smaller than Σ₂₂.

items.stem: X is exponential with mean 1/λ, and given X = x, Y is Poisson with mean 2x. Then Var(Y) equals
items.explanation: By the law of total variance, Var(Y) = E[Var(Y | X)] + Var[E(Y | X)] = E(2X) + Var(2X) = 2/λ + 4/λ² = (2λ + 4)/λ². Trap: dropping the Var(2X) term leaves only 2/λ, the mean of Y.
